questions.stem_text:
Of the following page-replacement policies, which is guaranteed to incur the minimum
number of page faults?

options.A: Replace the page whose next reference will be the longest time in the future.
options.B: Replace the page whose next reference will be the shortest time in the future.
options.C: Replace the page whose most recent reference was the shortest time in the past.
options.D: Replace the page whose most recent reference was the longest time in the past.

questions.answer_explanation: This answer is correct because replacing the page with the next reference farthest in the future minimizes the risk of evicting a page that will be needed sooner, thereby reducing the total number of page faults.

questions.stem_text: Which of the following is the hexadecimal representation of the decimal number 231_{10} ?
questions.answer_explanation: The correct answer is E7_{16} because when converting the decimal number 231 to hexadecimal, it equals 14 in the first digit (E) and 7 in the second digit, resulting in the hexadecimal representation E7.

questions.stem_text:
In Python 3, which of the following function removes all leading and trailing whitespace
in string?
questions.answer_explanation: The `strip([chars])` function in Python 3 is specifically designed to remove all leading and trailing whitespace characters from a string, making it the correct answer for this question.

questions.stem_text:
In the Internet Protocol (IP) suite of protocols, which of the following best describes
the purpose of the Address Resolution Protocol?

options.A: To translate Web addresses to host names
options.B: To determine the IP address of a given host name
options.C: To determine the hardware address of a given host name
options.D: To determine the hardware address of a given IP address

questions.answer_explanation: The Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) is designed to map IP addresses to their corresponding hardware (MAC) addresses, enabling devices on a local network to locate each other and communicate effectively.

questions.stem_text:
Which of the following best describes the primary way in which a distributed denial-
ofservice (D D o S) attack differs from a denial-ofservice (D o S) attack?

options.B: The number of computers being attacked
options.C: The number of computers launching the attack
options.D: The time period in which the attack occurs

questions.answer_explanation: The primary distinction between a DDoS attack and a DoS attack lies in the fact that a DDoS attack is executed using multiple compromised computers, which significantly amplifies its scale and impact compared to a DoS attack that typically originates from a single source.

questions.stem_text: Merge sort has a running time that is least dependent on the initial ordering of the input data compared to other sorting algorithms.
questions.answer_explanation: Merge sort consistently divides the input data into halves and processes them in a manner that does not vary with the initial ordering, resulting in a time complexity of O(n log n) regardless of whether the data is sorted, reversed, or randomly ordered.

questions.stem_text: The access matrix approach can easily express complex protection requirements without limitation.
questions.answer_explanation: The access matrix approach, while useful for representing access rights, can become unwieldy and inefficient for complex protection requirements due to its inability to handle dynamic access control and fine-grained permissions effectively.

questions.stem_text: Finding a largest clique in an undirected graph G is known to be solvable in polynomial time.
questions.answer_explanation: Finding a largest clique in an undirected graph is NP-hard, meaning there is no known polynomial-time algorithm to solve this problem for all instances.

questions.stem_text: A program that has been extensively tested may still contain undetected bugs.
questions.answer_explanation: Even with extensive testing, it is impossible to guarantee that all potential bugs are identified due to the complexity of software systems, the limitations of testing methods, and the presence of edge cases that may not be encountered during testing.

questions.stem_text: Python variable names are not case-sensitive, treating all variations of the same name as the same identifier.
questions.answer_explanation: Python variable names are case-sensitive, meaning that variables named "Variable", "variable", and "VARIABLE" are treated as distinct identifiers.
